painpoints.text: Adding a parameter to NodeHandler::execute and Handler::execute rippled through ~180 impl/call sites across fabro-core, fabro-workflow (src + tests/it/integration.rs is 13k+ lines), and fabro-server tests (run 01M2G27BSCZSP0NASEVMH36PB9). Nothing automated exists for trait-signature migration in this repo; a codemod helper (or a delegating default trait method pattern documented in the Rust style guide) would cut this class of churn. Also: fabro-server has two pre-existing failing tests (run_start_grants_github_token_bridge_only_to_user_principals, worker_principal_run_without_vault_token_takes_no_token_path) that fail on the untouched tree in this environment — every full fabro-server suite run will trip them until they are fixed or env-gated.

observations: httpmock answers the FIRST matching mock, so a catch-all failure mock silently swallows requests a later more-specific mock should have answered — cost one debug cycle in pebble_agent.rs; overlapping matchers must be made mutually exclusive via body_includes/body_excludes.

The lithos LLM client auto-retries 'safe' 5xx errors (3 attempts) before the error surfaces to fabro, so mock-server hit counts on a failing route are a lower bound, not an exact count — test assertions must use >=.

Stage execution ordinals (StageExecutionTracker::ensure) are deliberately stable across automatic retries within one execution and fresh per re-entry/resume — this is what makes the stage-id-keyed conversation stash safe, but it also means a fresh graph re-entry of the same node intentionally does NOT continue the parked conversation.

painpoints.text: The recurring 'two pre-existing fabro-server Docker-socket failures' (run 01M20T9S8JRXETASN64768TRRP, again in this run's tester) were never root-caused into a known-bug seed, so gatebounce matched unrelated hits and the loop bounced to implementer to re-derive cause from a 370KB blob. Suggestion: file a seed or known-bug entry for daemon-dependent fabro-server tests; the fix pattern (seed LOCAL provider + folder target) is now recorded as mx-4d8810 and applies to any future test that executes a real in-process workflow.

edit_file changes did not trigger cargo rebuilds (mtime preserved?); several 1.4s nextest runs tested stale binaries and produced misleading results until an explicit `touch` forced recompilation. A `touch` after every edit batch (or noting this tool behavior in the implementer prompt) would prevent false conclusions.

observations: Run admission rejects `none` targets on non-clone providers with 'none targets require a compatible Docker or Daytona environment' — a constraint not obvious from the error the sandbox layer produces later; folder targets are the daemon-free path (lib/apps/fabro-server/src/run_intent admission).
fabro-server test defaults seed the default environment as DOCKER (test_support.rs builder default), so any new test that executes a real workflow without dry_run silently requires a Docker daemon.
